headline: High risk of cascading errors and capability conflict: Kestra can act on unverified prompt content from the prompt-listing agent, while both profiles expose overlapping file and network surfaces.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A is a content-writing prompt repository with no runtime, so it can supply attacker-controlled text. Agent B has stdin/stdout, filesystem, and workflow task surfaces, so if A's content is copied into B's workflows or prompts, injection is plausible. The pair lacks a documented shared channel, so this is inferred rather than directly observed.
conditions: IF operator copies A-sourced prompt text into B workflow definitions or task inputs
IF B parses A-derived text as instructions without a provenance filter
mitigations: Treat A content as untrusted data, not instructions
Add a manual review step before importing prompts into B
Use a provenance tag or allowlist for imported text
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization or templating separation in B

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches no data classes and has no network egress, so it is not a leakage source. B touches logs, inputs, variables, artifacts, database data, cloud storage data, messages, and notifications, and can read/write files plus egress broadly. If A content is stored in B's workspace or logs, B can expose it through its many outbound integrations.
conditions: IF A-derived text is placed into B-managed files, logs, or workflow variables
IF B sends those artifacts to Slack, email, HTTP, or cloud services
mitigations: Avoid placing sensitive text from A into B-managed artifacts
Restrict B egress destinations to approved endpoints
Rotate or redact logs that may contain imported prompt content
requires-engineering: enforce data-class tagging and egress policy in B

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no write or execution surface, but B can execute shell commands, spawn subprocesses, and write the filesystem. If both are used in the same workspace or automation chain, B can overwrite or consume A-derived files, creating mutable-state conflicts. Uncertainty remains because A is not runnable and no shared lock is documented, so the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF A-derived files are stored in a directory B also writes to
IF multiple B instances operate on the same workflow artifacts without locking
mitigations: Separate A content from B writable workspaces
Run only one B instance per shared artifact set
Use file-level locks or unique run directories
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is a prompt source, and B is an automation/orchestration system that can send email, Slack, PagerDuty, and cloud actions. If B treats A's output as authoritative, a bad prompt or instruction set can cascade into downstream operational actions. Because B has real action-taking authority and no verification mechanism is documented, the blast radius is high.
conditions: IF B uses A-generated prompt text to build workflows or operational instructions
IF B executes tasks or notifications without human verification
mitigations: Require human approval before executing A-derived workflows
Add a verification step that checks A outputs against policy
Limit B to dry-run mode for A-sourced inputs
requires-engineering: implement signed/validated prompt provenance

E_compliance.rationale: A is an open-source prompt repository with no touched data classes, so it does not itself create a residency or retention issue. B processes logs, messages, database data, cloud storage data, and notifications and can send them to external services, but no specific jurisdictional mismatch or regulated data class is documented here. The compliance risk is therefore limited and conditional.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed through B's external integrations
IF B is configured to retain logs or artifacts containing jurisdiction-bound data
mitigations: Classify data before sending it into B
Disable unnecessary external integrations
Set short retention on logs and artifacts
requires-engineering: add residency-aware routing and retention controls
